newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin rules out hasty constitutional changes.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin rules out hasty constitutional changes.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, making his first radio address since he fell ill with pneumonia, made clear on Friday he would not allow constitutional amendments sought by his political foes to reduce his powers or oust him.
"Amendments and additions can be made to (the constitution) but you should not rush this. It must be a natural process," Yeltsin said.

Communist opposition leaders are seeking to oust 66-year-old president on health grounds. He has had at least two heart attacks, he had heart surgery last November and he spent 12 days in hospital with pneumonia last month.
Yeltsin's poor health has also prompted concern over the constitution, which was approved in a nationwide referendum in December 1993 and which gives the president vast powers.

Proposals included allowing Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to serve as president until the end of Yeltsin's scheduled term if Yeltsin dies in office, reducing the president's powers, setting up a state council to govern or having the next president chosen by Yeltsin.

Yeltsin has appeared on television several times since he left hospital on January 20 but he had not made a radio address before Friday. One of his doctors said on Wednesday he needed at least 10 more days to recover fully.
